questions.correct_answer: A trapezoid with exactly one pair of parallel sides

questions.skill: Draw quadrilaterals and triangles with given conditions
questions.response: draw on the figure and write an answer
questions.prompt: Draw a rectangle that is not a square. Write its side lengths.
questions.prompt_markup:
Draw a rectangle that is not a square.
Write its side lengths.
questions.correct_answer: Two different lengths that match the drawing, for example 6 units by 3 units
questions.drawing_answer: A rectangle drawn along grid lines with two different side lengths
questions.grading_note: Grade both: four right angles with unequal adjacent sides in the drawing, and side lengths that match it.

questions.skill: Draw quadrilaterals and triangles with given conditions
questions.response: draw on the figure and write an answer
questions.prompt: Draw a rhombus that is not a square, with every side 5 units long. (Hint: a side can go 3 units across and 4 units up.) How do you know it is not a square?
questions.prompt_markup:
Draw a rhombus that is not a square, with every side 5 units long.
(Hint: a side can go 3 units across and 4 units up.)
How do you know it is not a square?
questions.correct_answer: Its angles are not right angles.
questions.drawing_answer: A quadrilateral with four 5-unit sides whose angles are not right angles, for example with vertices (0, 0), (5, 0), (8, 4) and (3, 4)
questions.grading_note: Grade both: four equal sides that are not perpendicular, and a reason that names the angles (not right angles).

questions.skill: Draw quadrilaterals and triangles with given conditions
questions.prompt: Can a quadrilateral have exactly 3 right angles? Explain.
questions.prompt_markup: Can a quadrilateral have exactly 3 right angles? Explain.
questions.grading_note: The angles of a quadrilateral add to 360°. If three are 90°, the fourth is 360 - 270 = 90°, so it has 4 right angles.

questions.skill: Draw quadrilaterals and triangles with given conditions

questions.prompt_markup:
Draw a parallelogram that is not a rectangle, with a base of 6 units and a height of 3 units.
What is its area?
questions.drawing_answer: A parallelogram with a 6-unit base along a grid line and the opposite side 3 units above it, shifted sideways so the angles are not right angles
questions.grading_note: Grade both: the drawing meets all three conditions, and the area 18 square units.

questions.prompt_markup: A triangle has sides of 6 cm, 6 cm, and 6 cm. Can triangles of different shapes be drawn with these sides? Explain.
questions.grading_note: Three side lengths determine one unique triangle (here an equilateral triangle); every copy is the same shape and size.
